runs.text:
Look at a bank. It is tangled with plants, many kinds, and birds sing in the bushes there. Insects move through the air. Worms work through the wet dirt. The forms are different from each other. They depend on each other. Laws made them. The laws are simple.

There is Growth, and there is Reproduction. There is Inheritance, which comes with reproduction the way weather comes with a season. There is Variability, from the world pressing on a thing, from use, from the lack of use. There is a Ratio of Increase, too high, and it leads to a Struggle for Life. Out of the struggle comes Selection, and Selection makes Divergence, and the weak forms die. This is how it works.

Out of the war, out of the famine, out of the death, the high thing comes. The higher animals come. This follows.

There is grandeur here. Life was breathed into a few forms, or into one. The planet has gone on turning, one law holding it, gravity, simple and fixed. From that beginning, small and plain, the forms came. Endless forms. Beautiful forms. They are still coming.

Look at the bank. It is tangled and green with plants of many kinds. Birds sing in the bushes. Insects move through the air. Worms crawl in the wet earth. Each form is built a certain way and each is different from the rest. Each depends on the others in ways that run deep. And laws made them, laws that work around us now.

The laws are these. Growth. Reproduction. Inheritance, which comes near enough with reproduction. Variation, born from the world pressing on life, direct and indirect, and from use and from disuse. A rate of increase so high it makes a struggle for life. And from that struggle comes Natural Selection. And from Selection comes the branching-out of forms, and the death of the forms not fit.

So out of war, out of famine, out of death, comes the thing we hold highest — the higher animals, made. This is what follows. Follows straight.

There is a grandeur in it. Life, with its powers, breathed first into one form or into a few. And the earth has turned all this time on its fixed law of gravity. And from a start so plain there have come, and there keep coming, forms without end, and each one beautiful, and each one a wonder.

runs.text:
Look at the bank. Plants grow there, many kinds. Birds sing in the bushes. Insects move through the air. Worms work through the wet earth. All these things are built in different ways. They need each other. Laws made them, laws that work around us now.

The laws are simple. Things grow and they make more of themselves. What grows passes itself on. Things change, some from the world around them, some from what they use and what they do not use. Life makes more of itself than the earth can hold, and this makes a fight for room, for food, for life. Out of that fight some live and some die. The ones that live change more, and change again, and move apart from each other. The weak forms go under.

So out of the fighting, out of the hunger and the dying, comes the thing we call high and good: the making of the higher animals. That is what follows. There is no way around it.

There is a kind of largeness in this. A few forms, maybe one form, got the breath of life a long time back. The earth has gone on turning, the way it must turn, pulled by the same law that pulls everything. And out of that one small start have come, and go on coming, forms without end. Some of them are beautiful. Some of them are strange. All of them are still coming.

Look at the bank. It is tangled and green. Plants grow there, many kinds. Birds sing in the bushes. Insects move through the air. Worms crawl in the wet earth. Each thing is built with care. Each thing is different from the others. Each thing needs the others to live. And laws made them. The laws are simple. Things grow. Things breed. Young are like their parents, mostly. Sometimes they are not, because of the world around them, or because they use a part or do not use it. There are always more young than can live. So they fight to live. Some win. This is Natural Selection. It makes creatures spread apart into new kinds. It kills the weak kinds off.

So out of the fighting, out of hunger and death, comes the thing we call highest. The higher animals. This came from war. This is the plain fact of it.

There is something large in this way of seeing life. Life's powers were breathed into one form, or into a few, at the start. The earth turned on its fixed path, bound by gravity, turning and turning. And out of that one small start came many forms. They are beautiful. They are strange. They kept coming. They keep coming still.
